macros.name: bardimen
macros.doc: The value of the bardimen key is saved in the \bardimen command as ⟨num⟩bp; this is global definition and is overwritten when the next bargraph environment is expanded.

macros.name: barfor
macros.doc: The \barfor command creates a (rectangular) push button used to represent a single ‘bar’ in a bar graph.

macros.name: bargap
macros.doc: The gap can be access through the command \bargap; if gap=3, then \bargap expands to 3bp.

macros.name: barLabelsNoTU
macros.doc: For the case that a bar does not have a \TU key (no tooltip specified), the argument of \barLabelsNoTU, which is JavaScript function or a JavaScript string, provides tooltips for the bar.

macros.name: barLabelsTU
macros.doc: The \barLabelsTU can be used within the body of the document to change the method of assigning labels to bars.

macros.name: isdynamic
macros.doc: As a signal to the package that the current bargraph environment is one that is dynamic, place the \isdynamic command within the bargraph content, and nothing else.

macros.name: nbars
macros.doc: The value specified by nbars is saved in the command \nbars; \nbars is globally defined and is overwritten then when the next bargraph environment is expanded.

macros.name: presetinputfor
macros.doc: Use \presetinputfor to set any actions you require of your \inputFor commands; any re-definition of \presetinputfor should occur prior to the targeted \inputFor commands.

macros.name: presetsbarfor
macros.doc: The \presetsbarfor commands are a way of changing the appearances of the individual bars.

macros.name: scaleFactorDef
macros.doc: \scaleFactorDef is used to reset initial scale factor the next environment.
